learningObjective: Distinguish round-half-to-even (RNE) from stochastic rounding and identify when each is used.

canonicalClaims.claim: RNE (round-half-to-even) is the deterministic IEEE 754 default: round to nearest with half-way ties broken toward even. Stochastic rounding is probabilistic: round to either neighbor with probability proportional to distance, producing an unbiased estimator suitable for low-precision training.
conditions: Stochastic rounding samples a fresh random draw per value.
nonImplications: Does not imply stochastic rounding is always better — deterministic RNE is preferred for inference and correctness testing.
Does not imply hardware supports stochastic rounding uniformly — it is opt-in on some accelerators.

misconceptions.claim: RNE and stochastic rounding produce the same output values; only the process differs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Stochastic rounding produces different values probabilistically; RNE is deterministic.

misconceptions.claim: Stochastic rounding is illegal because it produces non-deterministic outputs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Stochastic rounding is intentionally non-deterministic per-value; production accelerators (e.g., some training chips) support it.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: Habana Gaudi / IBM training chip specs

misconceptions.claim: RNE always rounds down (floor); stochastic rounding always rounds up.
misconceptions.whyWrong: RNE rounds to the nearest neighbor; stochastic rounding samples between two neighbors.

misconceptions.claim: Stochastic rounding is a biased estimator that shifts values toward zero.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Stochastic rounding is unbiased in expectation; that is precisely why it is useful for low-precision training.

implementationFacts: IEEE 754 default is RNE (round to nearest, ties to even).
Stochastic rounding: Pr(round up) = fractional part; Pr(round down) = 1 - fractional part.
Used in low-precision training on some accelerators to preserve tiny gradient updates.
performanceScenarios: BF16 gradient accumulation with stochastic rounding can preserve small updates that RNE would systematically round away, improving convergence.
